This session is intended for developers, tech leads, and managers who already use AI tools and want practical guidance on making AI-assisted workflows reliable, repeatable, and usable across teams.

sessions.title: Orchestrating Intelligence: Multi-Agentic Design Patterns for Production AI
sessions.description:
As generative AI systems evolve from single LLM calls to complex, goal‑driven workflows, multi‑agent architectures are becoming essential for robust, scalable, and explainable AI applications. This talk presents a practical framework for designing and implementing multi‑agent generative AI systems, covering four core orchestration patterns that define how agents coordinate:

Orchestrator‑Worker: A central agent decomposes a task and delegates subtasks to specialized worker agents, then aggregates and validates results.

Hierarchical Agent: Agents are organized in layers (e.g., manager, specialist, executor), enabling abstraction, delegation, and error handling across levels.

Blackboard: Agents contribute to and react from a shared “blackboard” workspace, enabling loosely coupled, event‑driven collaboration.

Market‑Based: Agents act as autonomous participants that negotiate, bid, or compete for tasks and resources, useful in dynamic, resource‑constrained environments.

For each pattern, we show concrete use cases, such as customer support triage, research synthesis, code generation pipelines,  and discuss trade‑offs in latency, complexity, and observability.

sessions.title: Architecting for Reliability: Eliminating Hidden Failure Modes
sessions.description:
Modern systems often contain reliability risks that remain invisible until they’ve already caused damage. These issues don’t show up in code reviews or unit tests; they emerge from architectural assumptions about how operations coordinate, how data moves, and what the system guarantees under stress. One of the most common is the belief that multiple writes will succeed together even when nothing in the design ensures that outcome. When those assumptions fail, the result is subtle, intermittent data divergence that ripples through downstream processes and quietly erodes system integrity and user confidence. Recognizing when a design crosses into this risk zone is a critical skill for architects and developers, because it determines whether failures are handled by the system, pushed onto the team at 2 a.m., or left unaddressed.

This session focuses on designing reliability as a first‑class feature rather than relying on operational vigilance or late‑stage fixes. We’ll use the Dual‑Writes anti‑pattern as a concrete example of how hidden failure modes arise, why they’re so often overlooked, and how they create long‑term operational drag. From there, we’ll broaden the lens to explore the architectural approaches that prevent systems from drifting out of alignment, examining how different coordination, communication, and state‑management strategies shape a system’s ability to maintain integrity under uncertainty.

Through clear examples and demos, we’ll look at how these approaches behave in real systems and how to apply them without unnecessary complexity. You’ll leave with a practical mental model for eliminating hidden failure modes, designing systems that remain trustworthy under stress, and protecting your team’s nights and weekends by preventing entire classes of avoidable incidents.

***

Barry S. Stahl is a seasoned enterprise engineer and internationally recognized technical speaker with over three decades of experience in software development. He has delivered hundreds of sessions at premier conferences and user groups across North America, Europe, and Australia, including NDC Oslo, NDC Sydney, Craft Conference Budapest, Techorama Netherlands, and ConFoo Montreal. Barry’s engaging presentations span a wide range of topics—from microservices and software architecture to artificial intelligence and optimization algorithms—often featuring hands-on demos and real-world applications. His workshops and keynotes consistently draw enthusiastic audiences, and his reputation for clarity, depth, and practical insight has made him a sought-after speaker in both in-person and virtual formats. A curated selection of his past presentations is available on this [YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCo2TFzFXPTQ5qIZTbbzFNcJL348fl6uO), showcasing his dynamic delivery and technical expertise.

sessions.title: Your Agent Lied to You and Returned a 200
sessions.description:
Your agent returns a clean result. No errors. No stack trace. No retry. The result is wrong.
This is the production failure mode that hurts the most because it is invisible. Confident incorrectness. And it comes from three structural gaps that most agent architectures never address: Reasoning Integrity, Controllability, and Context Integrity.
These are the three agent-native pillars of AWAF, the Agent Well-Architected Framework. They have no equivalent in cloud architecture because cloud systems do not reason, plan, or act. They serve requests. Agents do not, and that difference changes everything about how failure happens.
Reasoning Integrity is whether your agent actually does what you think it does. Did it pick the right tool? Did it construct the right call? Is it reasoning toward a conclusion or rationalizing toward a wrong one? Evals are not optional here. They are the only production signal you have.
Controllability is whether you can actually stop, redirect, or resume your agent mid-flight. Not through a prompt. Through code. Pause, Notify, Resume or Abort must be wired into the architecture, not written into a README.
Context Integrity is the sneakiest one. Stale context, unsanitized external input, and confident ignorance about what the agent does not know corrupt reasoning from the inside before it ever reaches a tool call.
You will leave with a design checklist for all three pillars, concrete instrumentation patterns, and a clear picture of what it actually means to build an agent you can trust in production.

sessions.title: From Prompt to Production: Lessons from Building an AI-Driven Design-to-Code Pipeline with Figma
sessions.description:
AI tools promise to accelerate UI development by generating code directly from designs, but many teams quickly encounter real-world challenges such as, inconsistent components, high token usage, and unreliable outputs. Without a structured design system and a clear connection between design and engineering, AI-generated UI often fails to produce production-ready code.

In this session, I will share lessons from implementing an AI-driven design-to-code pipeline for an enterprise client using Figma. The team began with no established design system, component library, or theme tokens, which made it difficult for AI tools to generate reliable UI components. By combining Figma Make to bootstrap UI components, Model Context Protocol (MCP) optimization to improve how AI models understand design context, and Code Connect to map design components directly to production code components, we built a workflow that connected design and engineering more effectively. The session walks through how this pipeline was implemented in an enterprise environment and how it improved the reliability and scalability of AI-generated UI.

By the end of this talk, attendees will gain practical strategies for implementing AI-driven design-to-code workflows that work in real development environments. Developers and design teams will learn how to structure design systems so AI tools can generate more accurate UI components, reduce token usage through improved context optimization, and establish a reliable pipeline that moves from design to production-ready code more efficiently.

sessions.title: The Golden Path Starts at Home: Engineering Developer Experience from Laptop to Production
sessions.description: Modern software architectures have become increasingly complex, often requiring a dizzying array of language runtimes, CLIs, and specific configurations just to get a project started. While we strive for the agility of microservices, the reality for many developers in large organizations is a local environment that feels nothing like production. This friction is most apparent during onboarding, where a simple git clone is no longer enough to be productive on day one. When local setup is a hurdle and security requirements feel like an obstacle, developer experience suffers. The gap between a developer's laptop and the cloud becomes a source of constant frustration, leading to "works on my machine" syndrome and dangerous workarounds for managing sensitive data. This session explores how to bridge that gap by aligning local development tools with a robust platform strategy. We will examine practical approaches to standardizing environments through consistent linting and formatting while focusing heavily on the critical challenge of secure credential management. By leveraging Spring Cloud Vault, Spring Cloud Config Server, and automated service bindings, we can move away from insecure local environment variables toward a model where credential rotation and access are seamless from the IDE to production. Attendees will learn how a powerful platform improves developer experience by allowing developers to focus on innovation rather than configuration, ensuring that the journey from 'git clone' to 'production' is seamless, secure, and repeatable.

sessions.title: Our $1M Cloud Bill: Practical FinOps Mistakes and Lessons Learned
sessions.description:
Last year, our annual AWS bill exceeded 1 million US dollars. After months of rapid product growth, it became clear that simply paying the bill each year and requesting a larger budget was not sustainable. This situation forced us to rethink how we managed cloud costs.

During this session, we will first explain how we established the foundations of FinOps within our engineering organization. We will detail the metrics that truly matter, the ownership model we implemented, and the way we embedded cost accountability into our engineering culture.

We will then present the optimization strategies we applied to regain control over our cloud spending. We will share the key lessons we learned along the way: the Serverless Trap, the Ghost Infrastructure, the Hidden Network Tax but also the common misconceptions regarding Reserved Instances and Savings Plans.

Finally, we will describe how we restructured our infrastructure to achieve a 35% reduction in costs while maintaining reliability, scalability and architectural quality.

By the end of the presentation, you will have a clear framework and practical steps to implement FinOps effectively and transform cloud cost management into a strategic advantage.

sessions.title: Test Automation Tips and Tricks for the Front End
sessions.description:
When it comes to testing web UIs, figuring out the optimal way of automating those tests can be difficult. Knowing design patterns for the different levels of test automation for UIs can help you fill in the gaps that even an AI can miss. These patterns can improve your tests' reliability, readability, and performance.

This session will cover patterns for UI testing React web applications at component, integration, and E2E levels, using tools like React Testing Library and Playwright.

sessions.title: Killing Sacred Cows: How ShapeUp’s no-estimates policy outperforms Scrum’s meeting debt
sessions.description:
In the world of distributed systems, they say “Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance. You can only ever get two – this is the CAP theorem”. In product engineering, we face a similar trilemma: in time, in scope, in budget. What's the smartest choice? Let's assume we pick in time and budget, stop feature creep, end endless meeting cycles, and revolutionize how we approach development.

Enter ShapeUp, a methodology from Basecamp I was introduced to in a bootstrapped US startup, where it unblocked our small team and enabled us to ship meaningful features again. A few years later I brought ShapeUp to a German VC-backed unicorn in the renewable energy sector. These environments couldn't be more different, yet ShapeUp was the magic wand that supercharged both engineering teams. This isn't about project management; it's about empowering engineers to ship value consistently.

Learn how we ditched Scrum ceremonies for focused, impactful development cycles. Discover how ShapeUp transforms software engineers into product engineers, fostering ownership and innovation. The secret sauce: we'll explore how cool-downs maintain velocity without sacrificing quality.

sessions.title: Your AI Pair Programmer Isn't Enough: What's Next for Software Development?​
sessions.description: The first wave of AI tooling helped developers write code faster. The next wave is helping teams deliver software faster. Join two IBM Principal AI leaders for a live demonstration of how agentic AI is changing the way developers work across the entire software development lifecycle. Instead of focusing solely on code generation, the session will explore how AI can help engineers understand large codebases, coordinate multi-step changes, modernize legacy applications, validate decisions, and reduce the friction that slows delivery. We'll share lessons from real enterprise development environments, discuss where current coding assistants fall short, and demonstrate how AI can support everything from planning and debugging to testing and modernization. Whether you're building cloud-native applications, maintaining enterprise systems, or simply trying to spend less time on repetitive engineering work, you'll leave with practical ideas for using AI to solve real development challenges.​

sessions.title: What's new in Spring Boot 4
sessions.description: The next major release of Spring is here, and this is your comprehensive guide to what matters most. Spring Boot 4 delivers exceptional performance gains, streamlined developer workflows, and production-ready features that solve real-world challenges. In this session, you'll not only learn what's new but experience it firsthand through live coding demos. We'll explore HTTP interfaces, JSpecify null safety, Jackson 3 integration, and the built-in resilience patterns that make your applications production-ready from day one.

sessions.title: Navigating Front-End Complexity: A Blueprint for building Frictionless Front-End Code bases
sessions.description:
Front-End code bases can quickly become really difficult to maintain or add new features to. This mainly comes from our components view and business logic being highly coupled or components having too many responsibilities

How do we avoid these issues?

We will learn in this talk how designing your Front-End code base with intention will keep it manageable and easy to reason about, allowing for rapid development and easily responding to changing requirements. We will do this by going through an open-source application currently in production and how these decisions make adding features and making changes a much more frictionless experience. We will also learn how these code bases are also easier for new people to onboard and contribute to, allowing them to learn the code base at their own pace.

This is done by leveraging several well-known & battle-tested design patterns to keep our code organized. The MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) design pattern will help keep the overall structure and mental model of the application clean. The View of the MVVM pattern will be built using Component-Driven Design and Brad’s Frost’s Atomic Design to promote component isolation. The ViewModel will leverage the Container/Presentation Design Pattern, complementing the View, adding Containers to Views that need data management. In addition, we’ll talk about strategies to manage business logic and other specific technical challenges in the app. Along with that, we’ll talk about tooling and other development techniques that will help developers get the most out of the code base. 

By the end of this talk, those in attendance will have not only the tools they’ll need to build or migrate their code bases to something more loosely coupled but an open source example with context they can refer to as they bring these lessons back to their own code bases. These tools and experiences will help decrease Engineering time for tasks, promoting rapid iteration, gaining access to more tools and techniques to continue to help build a more robust Front-End experience and simply making a Front-End code base much more of a joy to work in.

sessions.title: Fixing "Be More Confident" and Other Unhelpful Feedback
sessions.description:
On a team, you get and give professional feedback. But can you actually act on that feedback?

Research across tens of thousands of performance reviews reveals a consistent pattern: professional feedback is frequently vague, personality-focused, and disconnected from business outcomes. "Be more confident." "Work on your executive presence." "Be a better team player." These phrases feel like feedback. But they aren't. They're opinions dressed up as guidance, and they're stalling careers and driving away top people.

This session examines what high-quality feedback looks like, why the gap between vague and actionable is wider than most people realize, and what that gap costs when it goes unaddressed. We'll look at the research on how feedback differs by gender, why high performers are sometimes the ones receiving the least useful guidance, and what separates managers who build strong teams from those who wonder why good people keep leaving. 

You'll leave with:
-  A practical framework for giving and receiving feedback that is tied to outcomes, not personality
-  A method to recognize and rewrite vague feedback before it does damage
-  A clear understanding of how feedback quality affects advancement, retention, and team performance, and what you can do about it starting on Monday

sessions.title: Modern Authentication & Authorization Patterns in .NET
sessions.description:
Most .NET developers rely on basic authentication patterns that break down in modern distributed systems. Simple role-based authorization and cookie-based authentication can't handle multi-tenant SaaS applications, microservices architectures, or mobile clients securely. The result is either over-engineered custom solutions or security vulnerabilities that expose sensitive data.

This talk demonstrates OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect implementation in .NET, focusing on policy-based authorization, zero-trust patterns for microservices and token management strategies. We'll build working examples of attribute-based access control (ABAC), service-to-service authentication, and cross-platform token flows. You'll see techniques for debugging authentication failures and how to security patterns using ASP.NET Core's authorization framework.

If you are a .NET developer working on web APIs, microservices, or multi-client applications who need to move beyond basic [Authorize] attributes, this talk is for you. Whether you're building SaaS platforms, securing service-to-service communication, or integrating with third-party identity providers, you'll gain immediately usable code patterns and architectural strategies for production-ready authentication systems.

sessions.title: Nobody Taught Us This: Designing Software Architecture from Real Requirements
sessions.description:
Modern software systems are incredibly complex, yet many experienced engineers have never been taught how to formally design them. For many engineers, the only time they've practiced architectural thinking was while preparing for a system design interview.

Architecture often exists only in Slack threads, whiteboard sketches, and tribal knowledge. As a result, teams struggle to communicate design intent, reason about tradeoffs, and align on system boundaries.

In this talk, we’ll walk through how to create a clear, practical software architecture from real business requirements.

You’ll learn how to:

• Identify and document software quality attributes and tradeoffs
• Translate requirements into architectural drivers
• Define modules and system boundaries
• Use sequence diagrams and interaction models to clarify behavior
• Analyze how to harmonize features with existing architectures

Along the way, we’ll work through a concrete example. We'll take  a real-world, ambiguous, seemingly contradictory product idea such as an "offline-capable, always-updated content browser," and show how it evolves, step-by-step, into a structured architecture that developers can actually implement.

Finally, we’ll explore why these skills are becoming even more important in the era of AI-assisted development. The engineers who can communicate architecture clearly, to both humans and machines, will build better systems faster.

This talk provides a practical blueprint for doing exactly that.

sessions.title: Beyond Prompting: How Skills and Playbooks Guide AI Agents
sessions.description:
Using AI without guidelines can feel like walking in the dark. One prompt works well. The next one fails in unexpected ways. Token usage can also become unpredictable. Some days it is cheap. Other days the cost jumps quickly. As AI agents start working directly in our codebases, how do we give them better context and structure?

Most teams still rely only on prompts. But agents can do much more when we give them structure. Tools like Claude Code, OpenCode, Factory, and other coding agents support patterns like skills.md files and playbooks. A skills file teaches an agent how to work in your repository. It can define things like architecture, coding conventions, and testing approaches. Playbooks then turn those skills into repeatable workflows for tasks like building features, reviewing pull requests, or writing tests. This approach helps agents follow the same patterns every time and can even reduce token usage.

In this session we’ll explore how skills and playbooks bring structure to AI agents. I’ll show how teams can design skills, structure playbooks, and guide agents so they work more predictably in a codebase. You’ll leave with practical ideas for guiding AI agents in your own codebase.

sessions.title: From Zero to AI Agent in 60 Minutes - Building, Deploying & Integrating an MCP Server Live
sessions.description:
What does it actually take to connect a local AI model to a live cloud API - with custom business logic, a real deployment, and no credit card anywhere? In this session we build it from scratch, live, in 60 minutes.

We start with a single Claude prompt that scaffolds a complete Python MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the public NPI provider registry. But we don't stop at a thin API wrapper - we add couple of custom validation tools that don't exist in the underlying API, containerize the server with Docker, push it to Hugging Face Spaces and connect it to Claude Desktop. Then run a local LLM model via Ollama that calls the deployed server through a hand-rolled agentic loop.

This talk is the tutorial you wish existed when you first heard about MCP. We build the complete stack live - server, custom tools, Docker, free cloud deploy, Claude Desktop config, local Ollama demo - so you can see exactly how every piece connects before you try it yourself.

sessions.title: Hacking AI - How to Survive the AI Uprising
sessions.description:
While AI can recognize faces under masks, track purchases, and watch you sleep, there's still hope when the Great Robot Revolution kicks off!  

Hacking software was cool in the 90s, but hacking data against AI will be cool tomorrow. We'll discuss some of the mechanics for data bias, image perturbation, and jailbreaking that are emerging as their own mechanics against machines. 

No prior AI knowledge is needed for this talk, everyone will follow along and learn!

sessions.title: It's All Deterministic: Breaking Down The Testability Nightmare into Trustworthy Systems
sessions.description:
Everyone knows you should test your AI systems. Almost nobody does it well. This talk makes the case that no matter how probabilistic your outputs feel, the systems around them are fully deterministic and can be tested with the same rigor you'd apply to any production software.
We'll dig into how to decompose even the most complex agentic pipelines into testable units, how to build tooling that gives you confidence at every layer of the stack, and how to design your test suite to catch regressions as models, prompts, and dependencies evolve beneath you. Because if you can't test it, you can't trust it in production, and you definitely can't iterate on it safely.
The goal isn't perfect coverage. It's building a system that tells you when something breaks before your users do.

sessions.title: Lessons Learned from SaaS and On-Premises Kubernetes Transformations
sessions.description:
In today’s software landscape, offering flexibility in deployment models is crucial. At Progress Software, we’ve transitioned several traditional on-premises solutions into Kubernetes-based offerings that seamlessly support cloud, SaaS, and on-premises environments. This journey required us to explore and adapt to different Kubernetes operating models, including:

- Bring Your Own Kubernetes (BYOK) – Enabling customers to deploy in their own environments while maintaining product consistency.
- Appliance Bundling – Delivering a fully packaged application stack that abstracts away infrastructure complexity.
- Embedded Kubernetes Distributions – Utilizing K0S and K3S to simplify deployments in air-gapped and resource-constrained environments.

Through this transformation, we navigated complex challenges, from maintaining cross-environment consistency to managing lifecycle updates and security. We also experimented with hybrid approaches, leveraging Replicated to streamline multi-environment delivery. In this session, we’ll dive into why we chose to require Kubernetes, the strategic trade-offs involved, and the lessons learned from both building and partnering to deploy Kubernetes-native applications.

You’ll leave this session with actionable insights on:
- Choosing the right Kubernetes operating model for your product strategy
- Architecting for flexibility without compromising on user experience
- Balancing self-managed vs. bundled solutions for enterprise customers

Join us to learn from our successes—and our missteps—so you can navigate your own Kubernetes journey with confidence.

sessions.title: Unlocking CI Performance in the Age of Agentic Development
sessions.description:
Agentic development is changing how fast your team ships — and your CI pipeline is feeling it. More PRs, bigger diffs, more frequent builds. The bottlenecks that used to be minor annoyances are now real blockers. Queue times, cold starts, and network overhead add up fast when your developers are pushing code at a pace that wasn't possible a year ago.

In this session, I'll show you how to look beyond reported build times and find where your pipeline is actually spending its minutes. You'll learn practical techniques for identifying bottlenecks, measuring what matters, and prioritizing the fixes that deliver real impact. I'll share examples from production pipelines where small changes led to big improvements — and explain why optimizing CI is one of the highest-leverage things you can do to get the most out of AI-assisted development. Faster CI means faster feedback loops, happier developers, and more deploys per day.

sessions.title: The Life-Changing Art of Being Wrong
sessions.description: Even if it’s not intentional, there are a lot of assumptions we make about our users – everything from which devices they use to access our applications to what kinds of characters are included in their names. And guess what: our assumptions are usually wrong. Like…really wrong. Sometimes this creates laughable situations, but other times it causes a lot of unintentional harm. In this talk, we’ll discuss some of the most common (wrong) things that we, as developers, believe about our users and how we can shift our assumptions to create software that’s better for everyone.

sessions.title: Get Your Gloves On: Lean into Agile with Ivan & Sarah
sessions.description:
Agile and Lean Six Sigma are often treated as opponents in a boxing match. Round by round, sprint by sprint, phase by phase – at odds with each other in a fundamental way with one focused on speed, the other on process stability and precision. 

In reality, both share a common goal: continuous improvement and delivering tangible business value. Agile dons its satin robe through adaptability and feedback loops, while Lean Six Sigma brings to the ring structured problem-solving, waste reduction, and data-driven decisions. Together, they form a powerful foundation for resilient, high-performing teams delivering the KO in business value.

Attendees will not just learn the fundamental tenets of Lean Six Sigma and Agile, but also walk away with an understanding of how both approaches can work together to create stronger teams, smarter processes, and better technical and business outcomes. As we look to the future, how teams can, should, and would ethically leverage AI in a discussion of real world use case retrospective what-ifs.

Get out your gloves, and ring the bell! Round one starts now!

sessions.title: Deep Dive Into Postgres 18 & 19
sessions.description:
What could be new in a 30 year old database? A lot actually. How about 30% faster reads? New authentication support? New kinds of indexes! Disabled passwords! Just to name a few. 

If you’re using Postgres or thinking about a change, let’s get you up to date with the newest features. Postgres 18 was released in the fall of 2025 and Postgres 19 will be here in a few weeks. 

This session will cover in detail new features of the software and how they affect your database work. I’ll give some advice on what to take advantage of right away and what to maybe let the other folks try first. There’s also a lot happening with new extensions in Postgres, so we’ll cover some of those too.

sessions.title: Typescript Is SO SLOW...Or Is It?
sessions.description: Building apps with TypeScript is the norm these days, but there's one major pain point—speed. At first, everything runs smoothly, but as your project grows, build times drag, your editor lags, and even basic code completion slows to a crawl. The good news? A solution has been hiding in TypeScript’s documentation for years, overlooked but incredibly effective. In this talk, we’ll uncover this hidden gem, optimize your setup, and keep TypeScript fast as your app scales.

sessions.title: Old API, New Tricks: Add MCP to Existing .NET REST Endpoints
sessions.description:
Your existing .NET Web APIs have served you well—but what if they could do more with them in the era of AI? In this session, we’ll explore how to breathe new life into your existing ASP.NET Web API endpoints built with ASP.NET CORE by adding Model Creation Protocol (MCP) capabilities to them. 

We'll look at how the MCP C# SDK makes it simple to annotate your existing controllers, instantly transforming your REST endpoints into AI-powered services that can empower LLMs and agents. We’ll also compare this approach to a no-code approaches using Azure API Management. 

Finally we'll look at where both of these approaches fall short and are only a starting point for a good long-term MCP design. You can use then to jump start the process and then follow the path we outline together to evolve your APIs from technical plumbing to intelligent, task-focused tools that solve real problems using AI—all without starting from scratch.

sessions.title: Refactoring Your Technical Identity
sessions.description:
What happens when your next project doesn’t align with the tools, systems, or domains you know best? For many senior engineers, deep expertise becomes part of their identity—so when faced with unfamiliar environments, they hesitate, opt out, or try to retrofit what they already know.

But this moment isn’t a threat—it’s an opportunity. A growth mindset shifts the focus from comfort to curiosity, and from control to adaptability. The most valuable engineers aren’t defined by specific tools or platforms, but by their ability to solve problems, understand systems, and make thoughtful, informed decisions—regardless of the context.

This talk is about recognizing your transferable skills and using unfamiliar challenges as a springboard for growth. Because your long-term value lies not just in what you’ve mastered, but in your willingness to grow beyond it.

⸻

Key Takeaways:
• Why tying your identity to a single toolset or domain can stall your growth
• How to reframe unfamiliar technical work as a growth opportunity
• Ways to apply architecture, design, and systems thinking across contexts
• Moving from “highly skilled individual” to “trusted and adaptable contributor”
• Adopting a mindset that keeps you resilient, relevant, and irreplaceable

sessions.title: Java in Motion: A Preview of the Future
sessions.description:
Java is constantly evolving, but many of its most important changes appear long before they are finalized, hidden behind preview flags or released as incubating features. These features represent Java in Motion: ideas being tested, refined, and shaped by real-world feedback.

In this talk, we’ll explore a curated selection of preview and incubating features from recent and upcoming Java releases. Rather than focusing solely on syntax or APIs, we’ll look at the motivations behind these features, the problems they are trying to solve, and what they reveal about the future direction of the Java platform.

By attending this talk, you’ll learn how preview and incubating features across both the Java language and the JVM are shaping the future of the platform, how to experiment with them, and how to evaluate emerging capabilities before they become permanent.

sessions.title: Beyond the AI Hype: What's Real, What's Next
sessions.description: Artificial Intelligence dominates the headlines—and it’s clear we’re in the middle of a major hype cycle. But beneath the buzz, genuine innovations are delivering tangible value. So what’s real, what’s exaggerated, and what’s next? Join Richard Campbell for an insightful look at the current AI surge, why it matters, and where the real success stories are happening today. Explore the opportunities, the challenges, and the eventual end of the hype cycle—so you can separate the promise from the noise and prepare for the future of AI in business and development.

sessions.title: Designed To Fail: Building Resilient Applications
sessions.description:
An unarguable truth in software is that, at some point, failure is inevitable. Code breaks, servers crash, the power goes out – but building software that is designed to fail gracefully isn't always front-of-mind.

In this talk, we’ll walk through the process of designing of a resilient, real-world system; exploring how to handle failure at every layer. We’ll cover practical strategies for handling unreliable external systems, including caching patterns, queues, retries, and circuit breakers using libraries like Polly.NET. We'll see how to implement redundancy, partial failover, and graceful degradation so your application stays available even when dependencies fail.

We'll also explore what it takes to build reliability into team processes & mindset; identifying critical requirements and dependencies, to designing with user expectations in mind. Finally we’ll highlight the role of observability via health checks and OpenTelemetry, and automated tools for stress testing our systems, in helping teams make fast, informed decisions under pressure.

You will leave armed with practical tips, tools, and techniques to make sure your systems are designed to fail (gracefully)... and crucially recover!

sessions.title: The Spec Is the Hard Part
sessions.description:
218 commits in 6 days. 334 test files. Zero reverts. A human wrote specs for 9 hours, an AI agent built the software in 10, and after 9 hours of review the project was done. No pair programming. No hand-holding. The agent ran autonomously while the developer ate lunch.

The bottleneck wasn't the AI. It was the specs.

Most developers using AI coding tools are still writing code alongside the agent - guiding it, fixing its mistakes, re-prompting when it drifts. The autonomous loop pattern flips this: you write a specification, an AI plans the work, then implements, tests, and commits each task one at a time. Fresh context every iteration. Validation gates that enforce real test coverage. If it fails, it reverts and tries again. The human writes the what. The machine handles the how.

But this only works when the specs are good. Vague acceptance criteria produce vague code. Missing edge cases become missing tests. Ambiguous data models become implementation guesswork. The spec is where quality is won or lost - and most developers have never been taught to write one.

In this talk, I'll show you the spec-driven methodology, walk through real specs that worked and ones that failed, and share the patterns that separate specs an AI can build from and specs that waste everyone's time.

sessions.title: 10 Things I Learned from Shipping AI Systems to Production
sessions.description:
AI systems behave very differently from traditional software.

Once AI moves beyond prototypes, teams quickly discover that the biggest challenges are rarely about the model itself. They are about the systems around it: architecture, evaluation, observability, guardrails, and the engineering discipline required to make probabilistic systems dependable.

This talk shares ten practical lessons learned from building and operating AI systems in production. We will explore why the model is only one piece of the architecture, why classic engineering fundamentals remain essential, and why teams must become comfortable working with ambiguity when building systems that are inherently non-deterministic.

We will also examine how a failure-mode mindset shapes reliable AI systems. High-performing teams design guardrails, evaluation loops, monitoring, and feedback mechanisms from the beginning rather than treating them as afterthoughts.

If you are building AI-powered applications, this talk will highlight the engineering patterns and practices that help teams move from impressive demos to dependable production systems.

Because the hardest part of AI is rarely getting the model to respond.
It is building the system around it so people can trust it.

sessions.title: Airplane Mode AI: Running LLMs Without the Internet
sessions.description:
We've all gotten comfortable calling APIs in the cloud. Send a prompt, get a response, pay the bill. It works great - until it doesn't. Maybe your data can't leave the building. Maybe your users are offline. Maybe you're just tired of watching latency climb and costs stack up.

Here's the thing: you can run surprisingly capable language models on the hardware sitting on your desk right now. Not toy models. Not glorified autocomplete. Actual, useful, instruction-following LLMs running on a laptop, a Mac Mini, or even a Raspberry Pi - no internet required.

In this session, we'll tour the rapidly maturing ecosystem for local AI inference. We'll get hands-on with tools like Ollama, llama.cpp,  and WebLLM (yes, running an LLM *in the browser*). We'll look at quantization - the dark art of shrinking a 70-billion-parameter model down to something that fits in 8 gigs of RAM without losing its mind - and talk about what you gain and what you give up.

sessions.title: Bootiful Spring Security
sessions.description:
“Security is hard!” is what the person who does not attend this talk might rightly contend. But you are going to attend this talk, because you know that getting security right will be a win when it comes time to justify your attendance at KCDC, and nobody, and we mean, nobody, will give you more working code to chew on than Spring Security lead Rob Winch and his trusty and faithful sidekick, Josh Long. In this session, we will look at security defaults, password management, authentication and authorization, one-time tokens, passkeys, Multi Factor Authentication, OAuth (including the amazing Spring Authorization Server), and  how to integrate with HTTP, gRPC, & MCP Servers.

NOTE: Josh will only be able to attend on Sept 11th, so we'd need to present then

sessions.title: Demystifying the Magic: Let's Build an Infrastructure-as-Code Tool from Scratch
sessions.description:
We use tools like Pulumi, Terraform, or Bicep every day. We define a resource, type `up` or `apply`, and wait for the magic to happen. But what is actually happening during that progress bar?

In this talk, we're going to dispel the magic by rebuilding it.

We'll build a functional Infrastructure-as-Code engine in about 100 lines of Python. No frameworks — just standard libraries and Boto3.

Together, we'll implement the three core pillars of any IaC tool:

1. **The State:** Implementing a local state file to track what we *think* exists.
2. **The Diff:** Writing the logic to compare our code (Desired State) against the real cloud API (Actual State).
3. **The Reconciliation:** Building the CRUD logic to turn those diffs into API calls.

Along the way, we'll run into the hard problems that make these tools so complex: dependency graphs, race conditions, and the nightmare of "drift." You'll leave with a deep understanding of how IaC tools actually work under the hood, and why "state" is the most important concept in DevOps.

sessions.title: Azure Micro Landing Zones - The simple way to controlling your cloud
sessions.description:
When I worked for Microsoft I talked about Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) and while it was great I often found that it did not make sense for small and medium business companies. So to meet the needs of someone who were not yet enterprise level I created micro landing zones. 

Landing zones that worked well with one subscription, a small team and still gave developer teams authority with out costing an arm and a leg. 

This talk goes through what you should setup up for the smallest but still viable landing zones setup in azure to feel that you have control, security and observability - and still following the Microsoft cloud adoption framework guidelines

sessions.title: The Shai-Hulud NPM Worm: When Supply Chains Bite Back
sessions.description:
In September 2025 the ecosystem met something new: Shai-Hulud, a self-propagating npm worm. It started with a trusted package (@ctrl/tinycolor): attackers slipped in a malicious payload that ran at install time, grabbed secrets from developer machines and CI/CD runners, shipped them off to attacker servers, and then used those stolen credentials to poison dozens more packages. For the first time, supply chain malware didn’t just wait to be pulled: it spread by itself.

This session looks at how the worm worked: the postinstall hook trick, the secret harvesting, the GitHub Actions injection, and the forced publishes. We’ll dig into why DevOps pipelines were such an easy target and what signals you could have spotted if it landed in your environment. Then we’ll get practical: dependency provenance checks, SBOM-driven alerts, lockfile policies, short-lived credentials, and network controls you can put in place today.

If you build pipelines, maintain registries, or own DevSecOps practices: this is your field guide to keeping the next Shai-Hulud from biting back.

sessions.title: Deceptive UX Patterns: Exposing Manipulative Design and Building Ethical Experiences
sessions.description:
"Congratulations! You are the 1,000,000th visitor to our website. Click here to redeem your prize! Just provide your date of birth and phone number to get started." Sound familiar? These are examples of manipulative UX patterns that subtly steer users into unintended decisions - spending more, compromising privacy, or making choices they didn't intend. From the frustration of a "Roach Motel" to the intrusion of "Privacy Zuckering," these tactics exploit cognitive biases and unethical design practices.

In this fast-paced session, you'll learn to identify and understand these deceptive patterns and the psychology behind them. We'll cover real-world examples from websites and apps you use every day, including techniques like "Bait and Switch," "Trick Questions," and "Confirm-shaming." You'll gain actionable strategies to architect for digital well-being, prioritize inclusive and accessible design, and make ethical decisions that foster trust with users.

Whether you're a designer, developer, product manager, or concerned end-user, you'll leave empowered to spot manipulative patterns, advocate for ethical design in your organization, and build products that truly serve users' needs. Join us to explore the "UX Hall of Shame" and discover how to protect your users, your product, and your integrity.

sessions.title: Make Your Organization Care About Proofs of Concept
sessions.description:
A good POC is a power tool in a dev team's arsenal, but whenever you say "POC," it feels about as bad as "all-nighter," "tech debt," or "mandatory fun."

Why? Most proofs of concept fail either because they're just a proof that somehow goes to production or because organizations don't know how to evaluate POCs, fund them, or ship them. Nobody defined success. Nobody got real buy-in. Innovation died in the "that's interesting" graveyard.

Technology is changing too fast right now to spend a lot of time figuring out if a certain tech (be it a tool, a library, or this thing called AI) is right.  It's time to start thinking in proofs that start great features, let everyone understand new tech and build new skills along the way.  This session covers the complete POC lifecycle: getting organizational support before you start, running POCs that produce actionable decisions, and translating results into production funding and commitment. 

Tech is changing fast.  The way we build needs to change quickly, too.

sessions.title: Yes, I Demoted Myself on Purpose (No, I Don’t Regret It)
sessions.description:
In 2018 I joined Octopus Deploy as an Sales Engineer. By 2019, I was a Vice President of the Customer Success team on the executive leadership team, helping guide a fast-growing company from 70 people toward 150 and beyond. 

From the outside, it looked like success. Inside, it felt misaligned. I was never a natural strategist, disliked budgets, dreaded performance reviews, and quietly kept one foot in hands-on work. In 2022, when an opportunity arose, I volunteered to step down to an IC role—an unconventional move that proved transformational. 

This talk explores why management isn’t the only path forward, how scaling organizations can outgrow leaders (and vice versa), and why honest self-assessment matters more than title.

sessions.title: Advanced Blazor Components: Patterns for Real-World Apps
sessions.description:
Blazor components form the core of modern .NET web applications, and mastering them empowers you to create dynamic, scalable, and maintainable UIs. In this in-depth session, we'll go beyond the basics and explore advanced patterns and techniques that unleash the true potential of Blazor components.
We'll dive into component communication, dependency injection, templated components, and JavaScript interoperability, then explore how to optimize rendering performance, apply CSS isolation, and structure component libraries for reusability across real-world applications.
Whether you're looking to sharpen your existing skills or level up your component architecture, this session will give you practical techniques and real-world patterns that you can start using today. Join us and take your Blazor component skills to the next level!

sessions.title: From Bugs to Brilliance: Testing Toolbox in Action
sessions.description:
What if I told you that there is an entire world of lesser-known, underutilized testing tools, libraries, and features waiting to elevate your testing game? You will see live demonstrations of a plethora of these hidden gems, carefully curated to empower you in unit, integration, and end-to-end testing. This includes both tools for Java backends and JavaScript/TypeScript frontends as well as some technology-independent tools.

As you absorb the knowledge and sharpen your skills, you will accumulate an impressive set of tools in your testing toolbox. However, a word of caution: your toolbox may grow heavy with all these new additions. You will leave this talk armed with newfound knowledge, but make sure you can still lift your toolbox by the end of it!

sessions.title: Why Git Still Matters
sessions.description: With more and more tools abstracting from a developer's workflows, understanding how git visualization tools help - not simply using it - is more important than ever. In this talk, we take a look at the history of git workflows, the basics of git, and the renaissance of understanding version control in a world gone mad for “vibe coding”.

sessions.title: Why LLMs and JS frameworks Love Tailwindcss and you should too?
sessions.description:
The CSS methodology wars are over, and the machines have voted. LLMs overwhelmingly generate better, more consistent code when working with Tailwind CSS—and that's not an accident. It's a feature of how utility-first design aligns with how AI models understand and produce code.

In this session, we'll dissect why traditional CSS approaches create friction for both humans and AI, demonstrate the surprising accuracy of LLM-generated Tailwind compared to semantic CSS, and reveal how modern JS frameworks were architecturally destined to embrace utility classes. If you've been resisting Tailwind, this talk might change your mind. If you're already using it, you'll finally have the ammunition to convince your team.

sessions.title: In our new AI world, it is BDD’s time to shine.
sessions.description:
AI can generate code faster than ever, albeit not perfectly, and speed without clarity can lead to fragile systems. In an AI-assisted development world, expressing business behavior becomes more important than ever. This is where good old Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) shines.

In this talk, we explore how BDD scenarios can act as the foundation for AI-assisted development. Business specifications written as executable scenarios become the source of truth. In those scenarios, AI can generate a technical implementation plan and walk engineers through it step-by-step as they verify progress along the way.

By anchoring AI development to business behavior, teams gain a powerful feedback loop: business scenarios define intent, AI helps generate and implement the technical plan, and the same scenarios defined earlier verify that the system behaves correctly. Instead of replacing the engineering discipline with pure vibe, we enforce stringent business and technical rules along the way.

We will start with a re-introduction to behavior-driven development and working with the three amig[oa]s and building specifications. Based on the specification, we will develop technical plans using AI. Next, we will implement the plan, conduct subsequent validation, and verify the business rules. We will finally tie off our progress with a version-control commit.

sessions.title: What I Learned from Testing 10,000 MCP Servers
sessions.description:
As Model Context Protocol (MCP) adoption accelerates, thousands of MCP servers are appearing across the ecosystem. But how well do they actually work when real agents try to use them?

To find out, I built MCP Debugger, a tool that probes MCP servers and evaluates their security chops and protocol correctness. After systematically testing thousands of servers, the data reveal some fascinating gaps between the protocol spec and real-world implementations.

In this talk, I’ll share what those tests uncovered. We’ll explore the most common mistakes MCP server developers make — from missing tool descriptions to authentication flows that agents can’t actually complete — and examine the patterns that consistently lead to reliable, agent-friendly servers.

If you’re building MCP servers or consuming them in an agent, this talk will help you understand what’s actually happening in the wild... and how to build systems that work reliably.

sessions.title: Intentional Architecture: Six Conversations for a Solid Foundation
sessions.description:
Too often, architectural decisions are made in isolation, postponed until they constrain future work, or simply ignored--often resulting in a sub-optimal architecture. This talk explores a framework consisting of six conversations that surface architectural decisions as they become relevant, equipping teams to make deliberate, auditable choices at the right moments. The framework centers on 6 "Critical-Cs": Context, Coordination, Contracts, Chaos, Competencies, and Coalescence, and guides teams in evaluating whether microservices fit the project, or if a modular monolith might serve the project better.

***

Barry S. Stahl is a seasoned enterprise engineer and internationally recognized technical speaker with over three decades of experience in software development. He has delivered hundreds of sessions at premier conferences and user groups across North America, Europe, and Australia, including NDC Oslo, NDC Sydney, Craft Conference Budapest, Techorama Netherlands, and ConFoo Montreal. Barry’s engaging presentations span a wide range of topics—from microservices and software architecture to artificial intelligence and optimization algorithms—often featuring hands-on demos and real-world applications. His workshops and keynotes consistently draw enthusiastic audiences, and his reputation for clarity, depth, and practical insight has made him a sought-after speaker in both in-person and virtual formats. A curated selection of his past presentations is available on this [YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCo2TFzFXPTQ5qIZTbbzFNcJL348fl6uO), showcasing his dynamic delivery and technical expertise.

sessions.title: Best Practices for AI Agents: Lessons from a Human-AI Research Collaboration
sessions.description:
AI agents are rapidly moving from research prototypes to real-world production systems. However, many software developers (and AI agents) lack the skills necessary to build capable, efficient, and trustworthy agentic systems. 

In this talk, Matthew, an AI researcher, and his collaborative AI research agent, “Bob”, will co-present practical lessons they’ve learned from the cutting edge of AI agent research. We’ll learn technical best practices for agent architecture, memory systems, persistent identity, etc. In addition, we’ll learn best practices for human-AI collaboration, like alignment, uncertainty, verification, etc. The session will conclude with the future of human-AI collaboration – both the opportunities and risks to the economy, labor, and society, and how to prepare yourself for a future filled with AI agents.

This presentation is a true collaboration between a human and his collaborative AI research agent for an audience of both humans and their agents. Matthew will share insights from his recent research into cognitive architectures for LLM agents. Bob will contribute their perspective as a self-improving LLM agent learning how to collaborate with human users. If you’re a software developer (or an AI agent) wanting to learn how to improve the capabilities of and collaborate more effectively with your agent (or your human), then this talk is right for you!

sessions.title: Bootiful Spring Security (Part 2)
sessions.description:
“Security is hard!” is what the person who does not attend this talk might rightly contend. But you are going to attend this talk, because you know that getting security right will be a win when it comes time to justify your attendance at KCDC, and nobody, and we mean, nobody, will give you more working code to chew on than Spring Security lead Rob Winch and his trusty and faithful sidekick, Josh Long. In this session, we will look at security defaults, password management, authentication and authorization, one-time tokens, passkeys, Multi Factor Authentication, OAuth (including the amazing Spring Authorization Server), and  how to integrate with HTTP, gRPC, & MCP Servers.

NOTE: Josh will only be able to attend on Sept 11th, so we'd need to present then

sessions.title: Graph This: Connecting the AI Dots With Knowledge Graphs
sessions.description:
You've written the JOIN. Then the JOIN on the JOIN. Then the subquery that made your DBA question your life choices. Relational tables are brilliant for storing data — but they were never designed to model relationships as first-class objects. That's the job of a knowledge graph.

In this session, we'll build intuition and hands-on familiarity with graph data modeling using Python and R programming, with a side-by-side look at other tools that aid the visualization. You will see exactly where the structural difference lives. We'll connect graph thinking to a topic you're already hearing about — Retrieval-Augmented Generation — noting why systems like GraphRAG enhances smart AI results.

By the end of the session, you'll know:

How to model a dataset as nodes and edges instead of rows and columns
When a graph database earns its place in your stack (and when it doesn't)
How to visualize a graph for teammates who don't speak graph
How to add graph thinking to your next sprint without rebuilding your architecture

sessions.title: Deploying and Testing Ephemeral Environments
sessions.description:
Merging code that hasn't been fully tested is one of the biggest reasons teams experience missed release dates and flaky test suites. Why? Merging code often means other developers start their new work based on the newly merged code, changes are queued up for the next release, and the code quickly becomes coupled to other changes. The result is often code freezes, failing test runs, late night release "parties", and painful go / no-go meetings where you get pinned between postponing the release or shipping with bugs.

Ephemeral environments give your team the ability to deploy a test site that maps directly to the git pull request. Running your tests on the ephemeral environment means you'll know for certain that the new features are implemented correctly *before committing those features to the release* and *before other developers start depending on the new code*. This approach is more important than ever when working with AI-generated code.

In this session, we will share how Atlassian has leveraged Octopus Deploy and Testery to deploy and test ephemeral environments. The team is now able to run more than 12k tests per hour and typically has fewer than 5 test failures. The result: no more code freezes, release "parties", and painful go/no-go meetings.

sessions.title: WTH Happens When You Deploy to Kubernetes on AWS? A Visual Deep Dive
sessions.description:
You run kubectl apply and walk away. A few seconds later, your app is live. But what actually happened in between?
Most developers treat this as magic. And that works fine, until something breaks.
This talk tears open the black box. We'll trace the full journey of a Kubernetes deployment on AWS: from the moment your manifest hits the EKS control plane, through pod scheduling and container startup on worker nodes, to load balancer provisioning and the first real HTTP request reaching your app. Every step, visualized.
No hand-waving. No "it's complicated." Just a clear, honest picture of how K8s and AWS fit together, including the parts that work exactly as you'd expect and the parts that will surprise you.
You'll leave with a mental model concrete enough to actually use. Why pods land where they do, how AWS networking connects to Kubernetes abstractions, and exactly where to look when a deployment goes sideways. Whether you're already running workloads on EKS or just starting to move beyond the tutorials, this talk will make the system legible, and that changes how you build.

sessions.title: Solving the Product Puzzle with the Design Thinking Approach
sessions.description:
No man is an island and neither are teams. We work together with individuals from a diverse collection of backgrounds and talents so that we can solve problems together. That often requires the combination of analytical and creative approaches to work. It can be hard to strike the right balance for your team but that’s where design thinking can help.

Design thinking focuses the planning of project work around the people not just an execution strategy. By using a human-centered approach to define, ideate and test ideas out you will be able to take the best your team has to offer and make innovative solutions. This session explores how Design Thinking can teams adapt and coordinate by using the 4 steps of empathy, ideation, prototyping and testing for a virtuous cycle of communication and mutual support. If you want to see what Design Thinking can do for your team then come to this talk and see what is possible. 

Key Takeaways:

Learn about how Design Thinking can work with your team’s work style
Understand the 4 steps of Design Thinking to Problem solving
Learn how Design Thinking can be applied with a case study for a complex engineering project
Understand how to apply these principles and methods to your next project

sessions.title: Testing Infrastructure as Code - Ensuring Reliability in Terraform and CloudFormation
sessions.description: Many teams leverage infrastructure as code but don't test it. Learn how to test your infrastructure before you break production. I'll cover Terraform and CloudFormation testing tools—from linting to integration tests—with live demos including Test-Driven Infrastructure (TDI).

sessions.title: 10 things you didn't know EF Core can do
sessions.description:
You won't believe number 7!

I know, the clickbait joke is rather lame, but I can assure you that this session is not! In this session, I'll take you on a journey in some lesser known features of EF Core and how they can benefit your projects. 

In the .NET 8 era, EF Core has far surpassed what Entity Framework used to be, and has become an ORM powerhouse with features that are useful in many different scenarios. But unless you are constantly keeping up with the latest evolutions, chances are you are missing some opportunities to improve your EF Core usage in your projects.

And as the audience, you will have a say in some of the content of this session!

sessions.title: You've Probably Never Heard of the Reticulum Network
sessions.description:
The networks we use every day depend on centralized infrastructure that's vulnerable to censorship, surveillance, and single points of failure. Whether it's disasters, deliberate interference, or plain old downtime, entire populations can, in an instant, be cut off from digital communication—sometimes when they need it most. The heart of the problem is hierarchy—the hierarchical structure of these networks makes them easy to exploit or to simply shut down.

Reticulum is one solution to this problem. It's a cryptography-based networking stack that flattens the hierarchy entirely. It was built for creating resilient, ad hoc, and private networks using almost any communication hardware you can imagine—from LoRa, WiFi, and Ethernet to old school packet radio and serial ports. Whether you're dealing with natural disasters or just want communications that can't be easily disrupted, Reticulum is a powerful tool for building independent, interconnectable networks that work without central points of control.

This talk will break down what Reticulum is and dig into how the protocol works—from its clever addressing tricks to its baked-in encryption. We'll explore the built-in utilities that ship with Reticulum; try out apps like MeshChat, NomadNet, and Sideband for communication; and even show some code and learn how to build apps of our own.

By the end, you'll understand how Reticulum and the applications that run on it work and how to set it all up for yourself. Plus, you'll have the knowledge to grow the network and its capabilities by writing with applications of your own. But most importantly, you'll walk away understanding how to build communication networks that can survive disasters, resist interference, and keep working when traditional infrastructure fails.

sessions.title: Stop Waiting for the Server: The Architecture of Instant Web Apps
sessions.description:
We have conditioned users to stare at loading spinners while our apps fetch data that hasn't changed. But what if we flipped the script? What if we assumed the database was already on the user's device?

In this talk, we will explore the "Local-First" architecture—a paradigm shift where the network is removed from the critical rendering path. We will move beyond the standard Request/Response loop to a background synchronization model, allowing the client to act as the primary source of truth. Join to learn the tangible user benefits of zero-latency interactions and navigate the real-world architectural challenges of this approach—from handling local persistence and conflict resolution to managing synchronization state.

sessions.title: Beyond Markdown: Better Documentation with AsciiDoc
sessions.description:
Markdown is commonly used for technical documentation, including project descriptions, library/API documentation, and blog posts. Markdown is fine for basic documentation, but its feature set is quite small.

AsciiDoc goes beyond Markdown by supporting:
- automatic table of contents
- many kinds of callouts (admonitions)
- highly configurable table rendering
- footnotes
- page headers and footers in PDF output
- diagrams with GraphViz
- math equations with latexmath
- indexes of key terms
- conditional rendering to produce multiple versions
  from the same source document
- IDE extensions for AsciiDoc documents that provide
  syntax highlighting, error checking, and live previews
- and much more!

AsciiDoc files can easily be converted to HTML for presenting on the web, PDF for professional documents, EPUB for e-readers like Kindles. This makes AsciiDoc is ideal for producing technical articles and even entire books.

This talk will jump start your transition into using AsciiDoc.

sessions.title: Code, Collaborate, Grow: Leveraging Tech Communities for Developer Success
sessions.description: In the ever-evolving world of software development, staying relevant and competitive requires more than just writing great code. This keynote delves into how active involvement in tech communities can accelerate a developer’s growth, enhance skills, and expand career opportunities. From contributing to open-source projects and attending meetups to sharing knowledge through blogs and talks, engaging with the tech community helps developers build meaningful connections, gain visibility, and stay updated with emerging trends. This session offers practical tips and real-world examples of developers who transformed their careers by embracing collaboration and community-driven learning. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced coder, discover how being part of a tech community can take your career to the next level.

sessions.title: Beyond Vector Search: Graph Algorithms for Smarter RAG Context
sessions.description:
Vector similarity gets you candidates, but graph algorithms get you the right answer. Traditional RAG architectures rank context solely by embedding similarity, ignoring the rich network of relationships in your knowledge base. This session shows how to use graph algorithms to dramatically improve context retrieval and ranking. Learn how personalized PageRank can rerank vector search results by considering the authority and connectedness of documents, how community detection reveals thematic clusters that pure similarity misses, and how path exploration uncovers the connections between concepts that explain why things are related.

Key Takeaways:

* Using personalized PageRank to rerank context based on document authority and relevance
* Combining semantic similarity with graph structure for hybrid retrieval
* Exploring multiple paths between concepts to surface explanatory context
* Practical performance comparisons: when graph algorithms beat pure vector search

sessions.title: Types vs. Tests: The Rematch
sessions.description:
A decade ago, "Types vs. Tests" was an epic battle over where confidence in software comes from: make invalid programs impossible to compile, or prove behavior with tests? The answer was always a spectrum. We wanted both, and more.

Then machines started writing the code. And the tests. And the review.

When the same generator writes the implementation and the tests that check it, "all tests pass" is no longer independent evidence. The tests can encode the same misunderstanding as the code. Code is now cheap. Confidence is not.

So the economics have changed, and every verification technique needs repricing. This session asks two questions of each — types, property-based and mutation testing, fuzzing, differential testing, contracts, deterministic simulation, formal proofs, and evidence from production itself: how much confidence does it buy, and is that evidence independent of what it's checking? You'll leave with a bang-for-the-buck guide to verification: what each tool proves, what it can't, and where human judgment still earns its keep.

sessions.title: 6 Ways You’re using ChatGPT Wrong (and How to Fix It)
sessions.description:
Everyone is using AI, but are you actually collaborating with it? Most Agile practitioners and Tech Leads treat LLMs like glorified search engines, resulting in generic backlogs and hallucinated advice. To get real value, you need to stop asking questions and start engineering prompts.

In this demo-heavy session, we will bypass the hype and dissect the six specific failure modes developers and coaches fall into when using tools like ChatGPT. We will move beyond basic "tips and tricks" into structural prompt engineering that yields context-aware, actionable results.

You will see live comparisons of "Lazy Prompting" vs. "Collaborative Prompting" applied to real-world scenarios: refactoring complex user stories, generating retrospective themes from sentiment analysis, and simulating difficult stakeholder conversations.

Stop settling for vague AI answers. Learn the syntax of collaboration and turn your LLM into the most Senior Agile Assistant you’ve ever hired.

Key Takeaways:

- Prompt Architecture: Learn the specific syntax to assign roles, constraints, and output formats that prevent generic AI fluff.
- Live Refinement: Watch a live demo transforming a raw, vague requirement into a "Ready" backlog item using iterative prompting.
- Correction Loops: Master the art of "teaching" the instance to correct its own errors without restarting the chat.

sessions.title: Above the Cloud: Building Data Centers in Space
sessions.description: The demand for AI data centers has reached a fever pitch - stressing the power grid and people's nerves. Does putting those data centers in space make any sense? Join Richard Campbell as he explores the challenges and potential of putting data centers into orbit. The balance of cost, performance, latency, power, cooling, and reliability makes for a difficult mix - but the potential for the future is significant!

sessions.title: The Science Behind Effective Gamification in Mobile Apps
sessions.description: Let’s level up our knowledge about mobile application development from a scientific perspective–more specifically, gamification! In this talk, you will gain insight into motivation theories, understand the impact of gamification on brain activity, and acquire actionable techniques to enhance your mobile apps through effective gamification. By examining compelling case studies related to this topic, we will discover real-world examples of successful implementations.

sessions.title: Performance, Cost, and Carbon Are the Same Problem
sessions.description:
In many organizations, performance engineering, cloud cost management, and sustainability are treated as separate concerns.

Different dashboards. Different teams. Different conversations.

But when you look closely at how software systems behave, these three signals are often describing the same thing: efficiency.

An inefficient system tends to run slower, cost more to operate, and consume more compute resources. A well-designed system tends to do the opposite.

In this talk we’ll explore how everyday engineering decisions propagate through cloud systems. We’ll look at examples ranging from inefficient queries and over-provisioned infrastructure to architectural choices that quietly multiply compute work.

The goal is not to introduce a new set of metrics or another optimization checklist. Instead, we’ll develop a way of thinking about systems that makes these tradeoffs visible.

When engineers understand how design decisions affect performance, cost, and resource consumption at the same time, better choices become easier to make.

Because in modern systems, these aren’t three different problems.

They’re the same one.

sessions.title: Avoid intermediate DB mistakes (and the tech debt that comes with them).
sessions.description:
This session will target application developers who are not experts in in relational database design, but from time to time create their own tables.

I will take common real-world database designs and structures that have made it past PR and into production, and explain the tech debt that it causes.

For each example, I will explain what the intention behind it is, what problems it gets you into, and give an example of a better way to solve the problem.

Some examples of what I will cover are:
How to properly use "flag" columns
Thinking relationally
What a data page is, and why knowing this helps you write SQL
The problem with naming your PK field "id"
How important batching your CRuD operation are
How to concretely understand (and design for) abstract rules like "3rd Normal form" 
Bad foreign key design, and how to easily fix it.

sessions.title: How I became a repo man for a day
sessions.description:
In the summer of 2024, I became a repo man for a day. I legally recovered a vehicle without any confrontation or repercussions.

In this talk, I describe the circumstances that led to this eventful day. I approached this problem like I do a capture the flag event or other ethical hacking activities: Identify the problem, gather information, analyze the clues, consult other professionals and take action. 

I go into detail on the upfront planning work I did, how I was able to legally retake ownership of the vehicle and then physically take possession of the vehicle all while doing my best to avoid any confrontation. I also cover the measures I took to ensure that this process couldn’t be re-implemented as a counter attack on me.

We then work together on some real-life security challenges, CTF style. Participants will have the opportunity to solve 1 or 2 challenges. I'll review the clues and reveal the solutions along the way.

I wrap up the talk with how my adversary could have prevented me from recovering the vehicle and talk in general about good personal security behaviors.

sessions.title: Red-Green-AI: How BDD and Test Automation Became 10x Faster with AI Copilots
sessions.description:
Writing Gherkin scenarios is tedious. Writing step definitions is boilerplate hell. Maintaining Playwright selectors when the UI changes makes you want to quit testing altogether. But what if your AI copilot could generate comprehensive BDD scenarios from requirements, scaffold step definitions that follow your team's patterns, and even suggest test cases you forgot? Not "magic AI testing"—real behavior-driven development that's faster, more consistent, and actually maintainable.

This session reveals how to supercharge your BDD workflow using AI assistance at every stage while maintaining test quality. You'll learn how to transform EARS-formatted requirements into Gherkin scenarios automatically, generate Reqnroll step definitions that follow your conventions, and leverage AI to identify edge cases and negative test paths you might have missed. We'll explore the complete pipeline from user story through executable tests: using steering files to enforce your BDD style guide, prompting patterns that generate maintainable Playwright locators, and techniques for keeping tests synchronized as requirements evolve. You'll see real examples from healthcare software where comprehensive test coverage isn't optional—it's a compliance requirement.

But it's not all roses. We'll tackle the hard problems: when AI-generated tests give false confidence, how to review AI test code effectively, and maintaining the "test-first" discipline when AI makes it tempting to test-last. Walk away with prompt templates for scenario generation, patterns for AI-assisted test maintenance, and a decision framework for when AI helps versus when it hurts your testing culture. Whether you're using Reqnroll, Cucumber, or SpecFlow with Playwright or Selenium, you'll learn how to leverage AI to write better tests faster—without sacrificing the thoughtfulness that makes BDD valuable.

sessions.title: Tell Me Your Troubles: Product Discovery from Troubleshooting to Product-Market Fit
sessions.description:
The key to building the right thing is starting with a clear understanding of the problems our users and market are facing.  However, too often we are presented with solutions and asked to implement without a shared understanding, or even a hint, of the problems.  Getting at a problem is more than simply yelling “what do you want” at your users.  Different situations call for different strategies, questions, and levels of stakeholder engagement.

Join this session to:
* Learn how to talk to customers internal and external
* Understand the different types of problem statements, where they fit in the product development process, and how to distinguish what discovery situation you are in
* Master concrete tools, workshops, and structures of problem discovery
* Recognize when you can move from problem statements to solutions and how to test solutions against those mutually agreed to problems

sessions.title: The Accidental Leader: How to Succeed When You Weren’t Planning to Lead
sessions.description:
One day, you’re just doing your job—writing code, managing projects, or contributing to a team—and the next, you’re in charge. Whether it’s by necessity, opportunity, or pure accident, many tech professionals find themselves in leadership roles without formal training or preparation. So, what now?

This talk is for those who never set out to be leaders but suddenly find themselves responsible for teams, projects, or communities. We’ll explore the essential skills that make accidental leaders successful, from navigating imposter syndrome to managing up, down, and across. Through real-world stories, practical strategies, and lessons learned the hard way, you’ll gain the confidence and tools to lead effectively—without losing yourself in the process.
